context: Hina-young writes a small blog post; shows it to Sakura for feedback.
purpose: Teen sharing online writing with mentor.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.jp: さくらさん、ブログ、書いてみた。
lines.en: I wrote a blog post, Sakura. Will you read it?
lines.style: Bright, eager opening. Quick lift on the request. Hopeful—testing the waters to see if Sakura will care. Slight breathiness underneath, waiting for approval.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.style: Immediate warmth. Quick turn-toward, leaning in. Genuine interest—no hesitation. The tone of someone who actually wants to read it, not just being polite.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.en: What do you think? Tell me honestly.
lines.style: Softer now, more vulnerable. Slow the pace. There's real stakes here beneath the politeness. Waiting—genuinely wanting feedback, not just praise.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 文章、すごく素直で素敵。
lines.en: Your writing is so honest and really lovely, Hina.
lines.style: Deliberate, warm. Land on 'honest' with quiet conviction. This isn't throwaway praise—she means it. Slight pause before 'lovely' to let it land. Protective tone, defending Hina's work.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.en: I want to keep writing. I want to keep posting.
lines.style: Steadier now. Quiet determination underneath. Not boastful—just decided. The voice of someone who's been given permission to want something. Small, sustained breath on the commitment.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.en: Your readers are going to grow. They really will.
lines.style: Confident but not performative. Lean back slightly—this is a prediction she believes in. Warm, matter-of-fact. The reassurance of someone who knows how good work finds people.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.jp: 本当?嬉しい、ありがとう!
lines.en: Really? I'm so happy. Thank you so much!
lines.style: Joy breaks through the surface. Quick, bright attack on 'really'—surprise and delight. Gratitude is genuine and effusive but not performed. Her whole body in the thank-you.
